batch: WL84 - Learned Material Rules: Rendering Qualification and End-to-End Utility Closure
status_rule: Frozen and committed before any new reference measurement, replicate, timing or evaluation of the evidence run. Full-scale probes (launch size, memory, GPU utilisation, wall time) run before the freeze and are recorded; their image values are not interpreted.
question: Does the unchanged learned ER closure satisfy the original rendering-quality requirements against an independently qualified reference, and does it retain a worthwhile local-rendering cost advantage?

inputs.wl83: 40657a5 (results), code 9e273ca / a11e452 / a883aef: render83 (scene, render_b, cmp83 plugin), render81 (lay81 reference plugin, masks, rel_l1), closure83_dr; WL83 learned states fit_<set>_L_<arm>_s8301.npz and DF fits on LabServer63 ~/rest_compiled83/results (read only); WL83 OUTCOME D is immutable

image_roles.test83_iid_1_L2: the sole WL83 ER_L failure (reference-limited: unc 0.0265 > 0.25 x err 0.1019)
image_roles.test83_iid_0_L2: predeclared passing control (same grazing light, iid material)
image_roles.test83_hard_1_L1: control: ER_L passed, E_L genuine highlight failure (negative baseline, not repaired)

arms: all WL83 render arms unchanged (C0_DF, E_DF, ER_DF, E_L, ER_L; WL83 compiler seed 8301 learned states); primary = ER_L

reference.definition: unchanged layered reference plugin (lay81), scene, camera, light, integrator (path, max depth 4), resolution 256 x 256
reference.budget: fixed (no adaptive stopping): two independent halves of 32768 spp each (65536 spp total, 16x WL83), each half rendered in chunks_per_half with distinct seeds
reference.independence: seeds 410000-480000: disjoint from every WL83 render seed (83110 + offsets <= 383,600) and below 2^32 / 7919 (Mitsuba sampler.seed is uint32; render seeds are multiplied by 7919); halves A / B and every chunk use distinct seeds
reference.uncertainty: WL81 Stage F estimator, unchanged: 0.5 x object relative L1 between the two halves
reference.staging_report: the cumulative per-chunk half images (8192 / 16384 / 32768 spp per half) are stored and the uncertainty at each level is reported (descriptive; the verdict uses the full budget)

evaluation.rule: WL81 Stage F, unchanged: per arm and image PASS iff object relative L1 (64-spp candidate vs reference) <= time-matched layered-reference error, highlight-ROI relative L1 <= 0.10 (ROI = reference luminance >= 3 x object median), and reference uncertainty <= 1/4 of the candidate error (else reference-limited)
evaluation.candidate: the stored WL83 64-spp candidate renders (provenance: bit-identical reproduction in stage A required)
evaluation.time_matched: time-matched reference spp = floor(64 x GPU time of the arm / GPU time of the layered reference) per 64 spp, both from the UNCONTENDED stage D medians; the time-matched reference is rendered with a new seed (time_matched_seed) and compared with the WL84 reference
evaluation.per_image_verdict: PASS / FAIL / INDETERMINATE (reference-limited) for every arm; primary ER_L
evaluation.reported: image-wide and highlight errors vs the new and the old (WL83) reference; old-vs-new reference difference; highlight-mask agreement (new vs old reference); candidate MC variability from replicates

replicates.note: independent 64-spp renders of the unchanged candidates (same scene, camera, light, integrator); report the distribution of image and highlight error and the fraction meeting the highlight threshold; descriptive, the verdict uses the stored WL83 candidate render

economics.per_64spp: uncontended (no other process on the GPU; recorded before / after): ray generation, trace (integrator.sample Python call), GPU execution (dr.eval wall), kernel-history GPU time, readback / accumulation, wall; first call (kernel compile) reported separately; closure binding (state -> Dr.Jit runtime) time
economics.time_to_quality: image error vs the WL84 reference as a function of GPU time and of wall time; t_REF(e) by log-log interpolation of the reference ladder; ratio t_REF(e_ER@64) / t_ER(64)
economics.rule: ECONOMICS_FAVOURABLE iff for every image: (i) uncontended GPU time per 64 spp of ER_L <= layered reference / 1.10 and (ii) the layered reference needs >= 1.10x the GPU time of ER_L@64 spp to reach ER_L@64's image error (time-to-quality); wall-clock results reported separately (Python tracing limit stated)

outcomes: E: stage A reproduction fails, reference halves inconsistent (reported), or GPU contention during stage D
C: ER_L INDETERMINATE (reference-limited) on test83_iid_1_L2 at the full budget
B: reference qualifies and ER_L FAILs on any of the three images
D: ER_L PASSes on all three images and ECONOMICS_FAVOURABLE is false
A: ER_L PASSes on all three images and ECONOMICS_FAVOURABLE
not_authorised: closure, compiler, representation, threshold, scene, camera, light or image-selection changes

pipelines.reproduction: render_t = the WL83 render_b path (numpy camera rays, host accumulation), used only for the bit-identical reproduction of the stored WL83 renders (stage A) and as a timing comparison
pipelines.new_renders: render_g: GPU ray generation (Dr.Jit PCG32, same camera and uniform per-sample pixel jitter, pixel-major lanes) and GPU per-pixel accumulation (float32 scatter-add per launch, sample-major lanes; float64 across launches); identical sampler, integrator, scene and BSDF plugins. Introduced because the full-scale probe showed the WL83 path spent ~63 % of wall time generating rays in numpy and ~15 % in host readback at 3-4 % GPU utilisation; it changes only the random stream of new renders (all new renders use new seeds anyway).

probe.note: pre-freeze full-scale probe (layered reference, 2048 spp, test83_iid_1_L2, WL83 pipeline): B 128 / 512 / 1024: wall 33.9 / 28.6 / 31.9 s, of which numpy rays 21.7 / 21.4 / 25.6 s, trace 6.4 / 1.6 / 0.8 s, readback 5.2 s, GPU 0.39 s; GPU utilisation 3-4 %; peak memory 1.1 / 3.0 / 6.9 GB
probe.gpu_pipeline: render_g, layered reference, 4096 spp: per-pixel float64 block_sum with pixel-major lanes cost 3.9 s GPU (5x); float32 scatter-add with sample-major lanes 0.81 s GPU (= path tracing alone 0.75 s; WL83 pipeline 0.19 ms / spp); wall 7.2 s vs WL83 pipeline ~65 s for 4096 spp; equal statistics (mean ratio 0.99983, equal distance to the WL83 reference at 1024 spp); B = 2048 uses ~6 GB
